idea: Our ramen shop wastes money because we over-order perishables and run out of staples. I want an inventory and budget tracker fed by our supplier invoices and a nightly stock count, so ordering decisions come from numbers instead of gut feel.

problem: We throw away spoiled produce weekly and still ran out of noodles twice last month; ordering is guesswork.
user: Me (the owner) doing the ordering, and whichever cook closes does the nightly count on a phone.
workflow: Invoices get entered when deliveries arrive; the closer counts key items nightly; before ordering I look at usage and stock to decide quantities.
success: Spoilage waste halves and we have zero stockouts of the eight staple ingredients over a month.
data: About 60 ingredients, two suppliers, invoices as paper or PDF; the nightly count covers only the 15 perishable or staple items. Two years of history would be ideal.
Prices change seasonally, so the tracker must keep the price per invoice, not one fixed price per ingredient.
constraints: Whatever we use has to work on the shop's old Windows laptop and one Android phone.
